tagline: Up the creek from Sedona, then the switchbacks to the rim.
intro: SR 89A leaves Sedona and follows Oak Creek up its canyon, one of the few streams in this high desert that runs all year, under oaks, sycamores and ponderosa pine and between red and white cliffs. In about 15 miles it climbs some 2,200 feet, from the red rock at the bottom up through paler sandstone and limestone to the basalt cap on the rim.
At the north end the road gets out by a stack of hairpin turns. The Forest Service advises that anyone who gets carsick may not care for them. In 1984 this became the first scenic road in Arizona.

moments.title: Slide Rock
moments.text: Frank Pendley homesteaded here and planted apples in 1912, on an irrigation system of his own that is still in use. The slippery bed of the creek makes a natural water slide.

moments.title: East Pocket Knob
moments.text: The summit rises 2,000 feet above the canyon in a single mile. A trail of 33 switchbacks climbs to a 1943 fire lookout, one of two wooden ones left in Arizona.

moments.title: Oak Creek Vista
moments.text: About a mile up the switchbacks, the overlook at the rim where the scenic road ends, and where Native American vendors set out their work.
